summary.text: Bryan Randolph is a Democratic candidate for the New Hampshire House of Representatives, Carroll 3, in the November 3, 2026 general election; he advanced from the September 8 Democratic primary.
A licensed social worker and mental health clinician from Moultonborough, he said in a Ballotpedia survey that he would focus on housing costs and workforce shortages in the Lakes Region.

paragraphs.text: Randolph earned a high school diploma from Wilson Area High School, a bachelor's degree from Ithaca College in 2006 and a graduate degree from the University of New Hampshire in 2013, and his career experience includes working as a social worker.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he and his wife moved to Moultonborough in 2013 after he completed graduate degrees in social work and outdoor education at the University of New Hampshire, and that he works as a mental health clinician specializing in anxiety and trauma.

Randolph said in the survey that his campaign would focus on practical, bipartisan fixes to housing costs and workforce shortages, including restoring and improving statewide programs that encouraged towns and developers to build workforce and single-family housing.
He also said he would work to address health care and child care costs and wants the state to invest more in public schools while helping them develop effective programs.
